title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Hinders the Role of Exercise Training as a Natural Activator of SIRT1
authors: Carmine Sellitto, Graziamaria Corbi, Berenice Stefanelli, Valentina Manzo, Marta Trucillo, Bruno Cha...
abstract: Exercise training increases SIRT1 levels, which boosts the body's antioxidant system. However, antioxidant supplements appear to interfere with this exercise-induced activation of SIRT1.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: The effect of an acute antioxidant supplementation compared with placebo on performance and hormonal response during a high volume resistance training session
authors: James Ackerman, Tom Clifford, Lars R McNaughton, David J Bentley
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: An antioxidant supplement was compared to a placebo before a high-volume resistance training session. The antioxidant group showed improved muscle performance and a blunted growth hormone response.

title: The Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Fatigue during Exercise: Potential Role for NAD + (H)
authors: John Mach, Adrian W. Midgley, Steve Dank, Ross S. Grant, David J. Bentley
abstract: This study investigated the impact of antioxidant supplementation on exercise fatigue and NAD+ levels. Antioxidant supplementation increased exercise time to fatigue and serum NAD+ levels, suggesting reduced oxidative stress improved aerobic respiration.

title: Resistance-based training improves mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in aging adults, independent of polyphenol supplementation
authors: Mathias Flensted-Jensen, Cecilie Moe Weinreich, Ann-Sofie Kleis-Olsen, Filip Hansen, Nadia Stenner S...
abstract: Resistance training improved mitochondrial capacity and redox balance in older adults. Polyphenol supplementation did not enhance these adaptations and may have altered some vitamin responses.

title: Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Cardiac Troponin Release in Cyclists: A Randomized Trial
authors: Lieke J. J. Klinkenberg, Peter T. Res, Guido R. Haenen, Aalt Bast, Luc J. C. van Loon, Marja P. van ...
abstract: This study investigated the impact of astaxanthin supplementation on exercise-induced cardiac troponin release in cyclists. Astaxanthin supplementation did not reduce cardiac troponin release after prolonged cycling, nor did it improve antioxidant capacity or markers of muscle damage.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.

title: Aerobic Exercise Training Adaptations Are Increased by Postexercise Carbohydrate-Protein Supplementation
authors: Lisa Ferguson-Stegall, Erin McCleave, Zhenping Ding, Phillip G. Doerner III, Yang Liu, Bei Wang, Mar...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of post-exercise chocolate milk, carbohydrate, or placebo supplementation on aerobic training adaptations. Chocolate milk supplementation led to greater improvements in aerobic capacity and body composition compared to carbohydrate or placebo.

title: Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Performance: “Common Knowledge” vs. Experimental Evidence
authors: Andrés Hernández, Arthur Cheng, Håkan Westerblad
abstract: This paper reviews experimental evidence on the effects of antioxidants on skeletal muscle performance. Findings suggest that common beliefs about antioxidant benefits may not be supported by scientific data and could potentially be harmful.

title: Tribbles 3 blunts exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation
authors: Ran Hee Choi, Abigail McConahay, Mackenzie B. Johnson, Morgan Ojemuyiwa, Brooklyn J. Phillips, Ha-Wo...
abstract: This study investigated the role of Tribbles 3 (TRB3) in exercise-induced skeletal muscle adaptation. TRB3 overexpression blunts exercise benefits, impairing glucose tolerance and metabolic gene expression, while TRB3 knockout improves glucose tolerance.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise: A Redox-Informed Framework for Training Adaptation, Performance, and Recovery
authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu; Andrei Tudor; Andreea Maria Mănescu; Iulius Radulian Mărgărit; Cătălin Octavia...
abstract: Antioxidants can hinder training adaptations by blunting exercise-induced signals. However, certain food-derived antioxidants may aid recovery without impairing gains. A framework called Redox-Adaptive Periodization is proposed to optimize antioxidant use based on training goals.

title: Exercise Training Combined with  Bifidobacterium Longum  OLP-01 Supplementation Improves Exercise Physiological Adaption and Performance
authors: Wen-Ching Huang, Yi-Ju Hsu, Chi-Chang Huang, Hsuan-Chen Liu, Mon-Chien Lee
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise training combined with *Bifidobacterium longum* OLP-01 supplementation in mice. The combination significantly improved exercise performance, reduced fatigue markers, and ameliorated exercise-induced inflammation and injury.

title: The effect of green tea extract supplementation on exercise-induced oxidative stress parameters in male sprinters
authors: Ewa Jówko, Barbara Długołęcka, Beata Makaruk, Igor Cieśliński
abstract: This study investigated the effects of green tea extract on oxidative stress markers in male sprinters. Green tea extract supplementation reduced exercise-induced oxidative stress without negatively impacting sprint performance or antioxidant enzyme adaptation.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: Diclofenac Administration after Physical Training Blunts Adaptations of Peripheral Systems and Leads to Losses in Exercise Performance: In Vivo and In Silico Analyses
authors: Rômulo Pillon Barcelos, Frederico Diniz Lima, Aline Alves Courtes, Ingrid Kich da Silva, Jose Eduard...
abstract: This study investigated diclofenac's impact on exercise adaptations in rats. Diclofenac blunted exercise-induced performance gains and tissue adaptations, despite reducing inflammation.

title: High-Dose Astaxanthin Supplementation Suppresses Antioxidant Enzyme Activity during Moderate-Intensity Swimming Training in Mice
authors: Yingsong Zhou, Julien S Baker, Xiaoping Chen, Yajun Wang, Haimin Chen, Gareth W Davison, Xiaojun Yan
abstract: High-dose astaxanthin supplementation was administered to mice undergoing swimming training. This supplementation suppressed antioxidant enzyme activity and downregulated Nrf2 signaling.

title: Housing temperature influences exercise training adaptations in mice
authors: Steffen H. Raun, Carlos Henriquez-Olguín, Iuliia Karavaeva, Mona Ali, Lisbeth L. V. Møller, Witold K...
abstract: This study investigated how housing temperature affects exercise training adaptations in mice. Thermoneutral housing reduced exercise-induced improvements in insulin action, energy expenditure, and body composition, indicating training adaptations are temperature-dependent.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and Dietary Antioxidants
authors: Abbas Yavari, Maryam Javadi, Parvin Mirmiran, Zahra Bahadoran
abstract: This review examined evidence on antioxidant supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. A balanced diet rich in natural antioxidants is recommended over supplementation for athletes.

title: (–)-Epicatechin Supplementation Inhibits Aerobic Adaptations to Cycling Exercise in Humans
authors: Neil A. Schwarz, Zachary J. Blahnik, Srihari Prahadeeswaran, Sarah K. McKinley-Barnard, Shelley L. H...
abstract: This study investigated if (–)-epicatechin supplementation enhances cycling training adaptations. The findings indicate that (–)-epicatechin supplementation inhibits aerobic adaptations, specifically peak VO2 and succinate dehydrogenase content, compared to a placebo.

title: Antioxidants and Sports Performance
authors: Vicente Javier Clemente-Suárez, Álvaro Bustamante-Sanchez, Juan Mielgo-Ayuso, Ismael Martínez-Guarda...
abstract: This review analyzes the role of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant responses in sports performance and training adaptations. ROS production during exercise significantly impacts performance, and antioxidants can aid recovery and performance.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: Exercise performance and physiological responses: the potential role of redox imbalance
authors: Kavey Vidal, Nathaniel Robinson, Stephen J. Ives
abstract: This study investigated the effects of hyperoxia and an antioxidant cocktail on cycling performance and physiological responses. Ingesting an antioxidant cocktail impaired performance, ventilation, and economy, suggesting a disruption of redox balance.

title: Vitamin A Oral Supplementation Induces Oxidative Stress and Suppresses IL-10 and HSP70 in Skeletal Muscle of Trained Rats
authors: Lyvia Lintzmaier Petiz, Carolina Saibro Girardi, Rafael Calixto Bortolin, Alice Kunzler, Juciano Gas...
abstract: Vitamin A supplementation was studied in trained rats. It impaired exercise-induced antioxidant capacity and suppressed anti-inflammatory responses in skeletal muscle.

title: Dietary thiols in exercise: oxidative stress defence, exercise performance, and adaptation
authors: Yanita McLeay, Stephen Stannard, Stuart Houltham, Carlene Starck
abstract: This paper reviews dietary thiols, focusing on their role in exercise-induced oxidative stress defense and performance. It suggests that thiol donors, like keratin, may enhance antioxidant capacity and performance without negatively impacting training adaptations.

title: Impact of exercise training and supplemental oxygen on submaximal exercise performance in patients with COPD
authors: Daniel Neunhäuserer, Bernhard Reich, Barbara Mayr, Bernhard Kaiser, Bernd Lamprecht, David Niedersee...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with and without supplemental oxygen on COPD patients' submaximal exercise performance. Exercise training improved exercise tolerance and capacity, with supplemental oxygen having minimal additional benefits.

title: Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress and the Effects of Antioxidant Intake from a Physiological Viewpoint
authors: Takuji Kawamura, Isao Muraoka
abstract: This review examines exercise-induced oxidative stress and the impact of antioxidant intake in healthy individuals. It finds that while exercise increases reactive oxygen species, antioxidant supplementation's effects are extensively studied but complex.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: effects of dietary antioxidants on exercise and sports performance
authors: Drew E. Gonzalez; Broderick L. Dickerson; Brandon M. Roberts; Jennifer A. Kurtz; Hunter S. Waldman; ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Following a comprehensive review, the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on the role of dietary antioxidants in exercise and sport. Antioxidants play a

title: Impact of pre‐exercise feeding status on metabolic adaptations to endurance‐type exercise training
authors: Robert M. Edinburgh, Francoise Koumanov, Javier T. Gonzalez
abstract: This study investigated how pre-exercise feeding status affects metabolic adaptations to endurance training. Performing exercise in a fasted state may enhance certain metabolic adaptations compared to exercising after nutrient ingestion.

title: Effect of endurance training and cinnamon supplementation on post-exercise oxidative responses in rats
authors: Gholamreza Dehghan, Mehrnoosh Shaghaghi, Afshar Jafari, Mustafa Mohammadi, Reza Badalzadeh
abstract: This study investigated the effects of endurance training and cinnamon supplementation on oxidative stress in rats after exhaustive exercise. The findings indicate that combining training and cinnamon supplementation offers the greatest protection against exercise-induced oxidative damage.

title: Acute exercise and oxidative stress: a 30 year history
authors: Kelsey Fisher-Wellman, Richard J Bloomer
abstract: Acute exercise can induce oxidative stress, with its extent influenced by exercise and subject factors. This stress, however, appears to be a necessary stimulus for enhancing endogenous antioxidant defenses.

title: Astaxanthin supplementation enhances metabolic adaptation with aerobic training in the elderly
authors: Sophia Z. Liu, Ana P. Valencia, Matt P. VanDoren, Eric G. Shankland, Baback Roshanravan, Kevin E. Co...
abstract: Astaxanthin supplementation was studied alongside aerobic training in elderly adults to assess its impact on metabolic adaptation. The study found astaxanthin enhanced specific muscle endurance and fat oxidation, particularly in males.

title: Supplemental Oxygen during Exercise Training in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
authors: SARA FAGGIAN, FRANCESCA BATTISTA, MARCO VECCHIATO, RICHARD CASABURI, MARGARETA EMTNER, NICOLA BORASI...
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: This review examines supplemental oxygen's role in COPD exercise training. Supplemental oxygen may benefit specific patients and conditions, particularly with high-intensity training, to enhance exercise tolerance and adaptations.

title: Editorial: Exercise-induced oxidative stress and the role of antioxidants in sport and exercise
authors: Hannah J. Moir, Marcin Maciejczyk, Mateusz Maciejczyk, Felipe J. Aidar, Hamid Arazi
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living

title: Chronic CaMKII inhibition blunts the cardiac contractile response to exercise training
authors: Guri Kaurstad, Marcia N. Alves, Ole J. Kemi, Natale Rolim, Morten A. Høydal, Helene Wisløff, Tomas O...
abstract: Chronic CaMKII inhibition was studied in mice undergoing exercise training. This inhibition blunted the improvement in cardiac contractile function typically seen with exercise, despite a paradoxical increase in maximal oxygen uptake.

title: Exercise, oxidants, and antioxidants change the shape of the bell-shaped hormesis curve
authors: Zsolt Radak, Kazunari Ishihara, Eva Tekus, Csaba Varga, Aniko Posa, Laszlo Balogh, Istvan Boldogh, E...
abstract: This paper examines how exercise and antioxidant treatments affect the relationship between ROS and physiological function. It concludes that antioxidant timing relative to exercise intensity dictates whether function is attenuated or enhanced, and that fitness influences this response.

title: Ketone ester supplementation blunts overreaching symptoms during endurance training overload
authors: Chiel Poffé, Monique Ramaekers, Ruud Van Thienen, Peter Hespel
abstract: Ketone ester supplementation was studied in endurance athletes undergoing training overload. This supplementation blunted overreaching symptoms and enhanced performance.

title: Effects of Resveratrol Supplementation and Exercise Training on Exercise Performance in Middle-Aged Mice
authors: Nai-Wen Kan, Chin-Shan Ho, Yen-Shuo Chiu, Wen-Ching Huang, Pei-Yu Chen, Yu-Tang Tung, Chi-Chang Huan...
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of resveratrol supplementation and exercise training on middle-aged mice. The combination significantly improved muscle strength and endurance compared to individual interventions.

title: The Impact of Exercise Training and Supplemental Oxygen on Peripheral Muscles in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: DANIEL NEUNHÄUSERER, MARTIN HUDELMAIER, DAVID NIEDERSEER, MARCO VECCHIATO, WOLFGANG WIRTH, EVA STEID...
source: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise training with or without supplemental oxygen on peripheral muscles in COPD patients. Supplemental oxygen enhanced exercise training's impact on peak work rate and muscle cross-sectional area, suggesting it aids training adaptations.

title: Effect of carbohydrate–protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations
authors: Abdullah F. Alghannam, Iain Templeman, Joel E. Thomas, Dawid Jedrzejewski, Samuel Griffiths, Joseph ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of post-exercise carbohydrate-protein supplementation on endurance training adaptations in men and women. Post-exercise protein supplementation increased mTOR gene expression, but did not enhance improvements in maximal oxygen uptake compared to carbohydrate-only supplementation.

title: Antioxidants to Supplement or Not to Supplement That Is the Question
authors: Stanley Omaye, Nabil Elsayed

title: Training Enhances Immune Cells Mitochondrial Biosynthesis, Fission, Fusion, and Their Antioxidant Capabilities Synergistically with Dietary Docosahexaenoic Supplementation
authors: Carla Busquets-Cortés, Xavier Capó, Miquel Martorell, Josep A. Tur, Antoni Sureda, Antoni Pons
abstract: Training and DHA supplementation increased mitochondrial proteins and activity in immune cells. This combined intervention enhanced mitochondrial function more than training alone.

title: Oxidants, Antioxidants, and the Beneficial Roles of Exercise-Induced Production of Reactive Species
authors: Elisa Couto Gomes, Albená Nunes Silva, Marta Rubino de Oliveira
abstract: This review examines reactive species produced during exercise and their impact on adaptation. Exercise-induced reactive species promote beneficial adaptations like angiogenesis and muscle growth.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Creatine supplementation post-exercise does not enhance training-induced adaptations in middle to older aged males
authors: Matthew B. Cooke, Brian Brabham, Thomas W. Buford, Brian D. Shelmadine, Matthew McPheeters, Geoffrey...
abstract: This study investigated creatine supplementation post-exercise in older males undergoing resistance training. Creatine did not enhance training-induced gains in body composition or muscle strength compared to placebo.

title: The Synergistic Effects of Resveratrol combined with Resistant Training on Exercise Performance and Physiological Adaption
authors: Nai-Wen Kan, Mon-Chien Lee, Yu-Tang Tung, Chien-Chao Chiu, Chi-Chang Huang, Wen-Ching Huang
abstract: This study investigated the combined effects of resveratrol and resistance training on exercise performance and physiological adaptations in mice. The combination showed synergistic benefits for grip strength, anaerobic capacity, and lactate levels, suggesting potential for improved health and physical activity.

title: Supplementation with α-Lipoic Acid, CoQ10, and Vitamin E Augments Running Performance and Mitochondrial Function in Female Mice
authors: Arkan Abadi, Justin D. Crane, Daniel Ogborn, Bart Hettinga, Mahmood Akhtar, Andrew Stokl, Lauren Mac...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of an antioxidant cocktail on running performance and mitochondrial function in mice. The supplement improved performance and mitochondrial function in untrained female mice, but not in trained mice.

title: Lower vascular conductance responses to handgrip exercise are improved following acute antioxidant supplementation in young individuals with post‐traumatic stress disorder
authors: Jennifer B. Weggen, Ashley M. Darling, Aaron S. Autler, Austin C. Hogwood, Kevin P. Decker, Jacob Ri...
abstract: This study examined vascular responses to handgrip exercise in young individuals with PTSD. Antioxidant supplementation improved vascular conductance during exercise in the PTSD group.

title: Combined effect of antioxidant supplementation and resistance training on oxidative stress markers, muscle and body composition in an elderly population
authors: F. Bobeuf; M. Labonte; I.J. Dionne; Abdelouahed Khalil
source: The Journal of Nutrition, Health & Aging
abstract: This study was aimed to examine the effect of vitamin C/E intake alone or combined with resistance training on antioxidant/pro-oxidant status, muscle strength and body composition in an elderly popula

title: Skeletal muscle BMAL1 is necessary for transcriptional adaptation of local and peripheral tissues in response to endurance exercise training
authors: Mark R Viggars, Hannah E Berko, Stuart J Hesketh, Christopher A Wolff, Miguel A Gutierrez-Monreal, R...
abstract: Skeletal muscle BMAL1's role in exercise response and training adaptation was studied in mice. Loss of muscle BMAL1 blunts acute exercise responses and significantly alters peripheral tissue adaptations to training.

title: The Antioxidant Role of Glutathione and N-Acetyl-Cysteine Supplements and Exercise-Induced Oxidative Stress
authors: Chad Kerksick, Darryn Willoughby
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This paper examines the antioxidant roles of glutathione and N-acetyl-cysteine supplements in mitigating exercise-induced oxidative stress. These antioxidants may help maintain cellular function and DNA integrity by reducing oxidative damage.

title: Effect of exercise and antioxidant supplementation on cellular lipid peroxidation in elderly individuals: Systematic review and network meta-analysis
authors: Chunxia Ni, Yiyi Ji, Keke Hu, Kai Xing, Yining Xu, Yanan Gao
abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis examined exercise and antioxidant supplementation's effects on cellular lipid peroxidation in the elderly. A combination of aerobic and resistance exercise with placebo intake most effectively reduced lipid peroxidation.

title: Mitochondria-Targeted Antioxidants and Skeletal Muscle Function
authors: Sophie C. Broome, Jonathan S. T. Woodhead, Troy L. Merry
abstract: This review summarizes literature on mitochondria-targeted antioxidants and skeletal muscle function. These antioxidants show benefits for muscle capacity, insulin sensitivity, and age-related decline, but effects depend on the specific antioxidant used.

title: Pterostilbene Enhances Endurance Capacity via Promoting Skeletal Muscle Adaptations to Exercise Training in Rats
authors: Jiawei Zheng, Wujian Liu, Xiaohui Zhu, Li Ran, Hedong Lang, Long Yi, Mantian Mi, Jundong Zhu
abstract: Pterostilbene (PST) was studied for its effects on skeletal muscle adaptations to exercise training in rats. PST supplementation enhanced exercise-induced improvements in endurance capacity by promoting slow-twitch fiber formation, angiogenesis, and mitochondrial biogenesis.

title: Antioxidative properties of phenolic compounds and their effect on oxidative stress induced by severe physical exercise
authors: Joanna Kruk, Basil Hassan Aboul-Enein, Ewa Duchnik, Mariola Marchlewicz
abstract: This paper reviews phenolic compounds' antioxidant properties and their impact on exercise-induced oxidative stress. Phenolic compounds can reduce exercise-induced oxidative stress and inflammation, but their effect on physical performance is inconsistent.

title: Effects of Peanut Protein Supplementation on Resistance Training Adaptations in Younger Adults
authors: Casey L. Sexton, Morgan A. Smith, Kristen S. Smith, Shelby C. Osburn, Joshua S. Godwin, Bradley A. R...
abstract: Peanut protein supplementation was studied alongside resistance training in young adults. The supplement did not affect muscle protein synthesis or strength gains in males and females.

title: Cornu cervi pantotrichum  supplementation improves physiological adaptions during intensive endurance training
authors: Wen-Ching HUANG, Chi-Chang HUANG, Hsiao-Li CHUANG, Chien-Chao CHIU, Wen-Chyuan CHEN, Mei-Chich HSU
source: The Journal of Veterinary Medical Science
abstract: This study investigated the effects of Cornu cervi pantotrichum (CCP) supplementation on mice undergoing intensive endurance training. CCP supplementation improved physiological adaptations related to fatigue and energy consumption, and maintained fat composition compared to training alone.

title: Skeletal muscle BMAL1 is necessary for transcriptional adaptation of local and peripheral tissues in response to endurance exercise training
authors: Mark R. Viggars, Hannah E. Berko, Stuart J. Hesketh, Christopher A. Wolff, Miguel A. Gutierrez-Monre...
abstract: Skeletal muscle BMAL1's role in exercise responses was studied using knockout mice and multi-omic analysis. Loss of muscle BMAL1 impairs acute exercise responses and alters training adaptations in muscle and peripheral tissues, potentially leading to inflammation.

title: Skeletal Muscle Redox Signaling in Health and Disease: From Molecular Mechanisms to Therapeutic Exercise Strategies
authors: Hyeong Rok Yun; Manish Kumar Singh; Sunhee Han; Jyotsna S. Ranbhise; Hanjoon Seo; Sung Soo Kim; Insu...
abstract: Skeletal muscle plasticity is modulated by a delicate equilibrium between reactive oxygen species (ROS)-mediated signaling and oxidative distress. Although excessive oxidant accumulation impairs excit

title: Combined high-intensity interval training and green tea supplementation enhance metabolic and antioxidant status in response to acute exercise in overweight women
authors: Elham Ghasemi, Mohammad Esmaeil Afzalpour, Shila Nayebifar
source: The Journal of Physiological Sciences : JPS
abstract: High-intensity interval training combined with green tea supplementation was studied in overweight women. This combination significantly improved metabolic and antioxidant status compared to training or supplementation alone.

title: Update: Is exercise-induced oxidative stress a friend or foe?
authors: Scott K. Powers; Mari Carmen Gomez-Cabrera
abstract: Exercise increases reactive oxygen species (ROS), which can cause oxidative damage. However, these ROS also act as signaling molecules, promoting beneficial exercise adaptations like increased mitochondria and antioxidant capacity. The net effect of exercise-induced ROS is a balance between damage and adaptive signaling.

title: The combination of exercise training and  Zataria multiflora  supplementation increase serum irisin levels in postmenopausal women
authors: Abbass Ghanbari-Niaki, Ayoub Saeidi, Mehdi Ahmadian, Leila Gharahcholo, Nooshin Naghavi, Mohammad Fa...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise and *Zataria multiflora* supplementation on irisin levels in postmenopausal women. Combining exercise and supplementation significantly increased irisin compared to a control group.

title: The effects of endogenously‐ and exogenously‐induced hyperketonemia on exercise performance and adaptation
authors: David J. Dearlove, Adrian Soto Mota, David Hauton, Katherine Pinnick, Rhys Evans, Jack Miller, Roman...
abstract: This study compared exercise capacity and adaptation with carbohydrate-rich, ketone-supplemented, and ketogenic diets. Ketone supplementation improved exercise capacity, while a ketogenic diet impaired it and reduced insulin sensitivity.

title: Individualised Exercise Training Enhances Antioxidant Buffering Capacity in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
authors: Tim J. M. Wallis, Magdalena Minnion, Anna Freeman, Andrew Bates, James M. Otto, Stephen A. Wootton, ...
abstract: An 8-week individualized exercise program was studied in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) patients. The program improved exercise capacity and antioxidant buffering capacity, suggesting a potential mechanism for exercise benefits.

title: Redox Mechanism of Reactive Oxygen Species in Exercise
authors: Feng He, Juan Li, Zewen Liu, Chia-Chen Chuang, Wenge Yang, Li Zuo
abstract: This review examines reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and antioxidant defenses during various exercise types. Moderate ROS exposure is crucial for adaptive responses, while excessive ROS can cause damage.

title: Cashew apple juice supplementation enhanced fat utilization during high-intensity exercise in trained and untrained men
authors: Piyapong Prasertsri, Thapanee Roengrit, Yupaporn Kanpetta, Terdthai Tong-un, Supaporn Muchimapura, J...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Cashew apple juice supplementation was studied for its effect on substrate utilization during high-intensity exercise. CAJ supplementation increased fat oxidation and decreased carbohydrate oxidation during exercise in both trained and untrained men.

title: Oxidant Antioxidants and Adaptive Responses to Exercise
authors: Paola Venditti, Mari Carmen Gomez-Cabrera, Yong Zhang, Zsolt Radak

title: The effects of physical training on antioxidative status under exercise-induced oxidative stress
authors: Eun-Young Choi, Youn-Ok Cho
abstract: Physical training's effects on antioxidant status and lipid profiles under exercise-induced oxidative stress were studied in rats. Moderate training enhances antioxidant defenses and reduces the atherosclerotic index, especially during and after exercise.

title: Comparison of the effects of two antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes
authors: Claudia D. Schneider, Patricia M. Bock, Georgia F. Becker, Jose Claudio F. Moreira, Adriane Bello-Kl...
abstract: This study compared the effects of regular and high antioxidant diets on oxidative stress markers in triathletes. A high antioxidant diet improved several markers of redox status in the athletes.

title: Impact of Polyphenol Supplementation on Acute and Chronic Response to Resistance Training
authors: Kyle S. Beyer, Jeffrey R. Stout, David H. Fukuda, Adam R. Jajtner, Jeremy R. Townsend, David D. Chur...
source: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
abstract: This study examined polyphenol blend supplementation's effects on resistance training adaptations. Supplementation increased antioxidant capacity but did not alter strength gains compared to placebo.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: Sake Protein Supplementation Affects Exercise Performance and Biochemical Profiles in Power-Exercise-Trained Mice
authors: Yi-Ming Chen, Che-Li Lin, Li Wei, Yi-Ju Hsu, Kuan-Neng Chen, Chi-Chang Huang, Chin-Hsung Kao
abstract: A power exercise training program was used to study the effects of sake protein supplementation in mice. Sake protein supplementation enhanced anti-fatigue activity and improved biochemical profiles in trained mice.

title: Training and Adaptation of Beef Calves to Precision Supplementation Technology for Individual Supplementation in Grazing Systems
authors: Joshua L. Jacobs, Matt J. Hersom, John G. Andrae, Susan K. Duckett
source: Animals : an Open Access Journal from MDPI
abstract: Beef calves were trained to use precision feeders for individual supplementation. The study assessed adaptation rates and feeding patterns of different calf groups to this technology.

title: Reactive oxygen species promote endurance exercise-induced adaptations in skeletal muscles
authors: Scott K. Powers, Zsolt Radak, Li Li Ji, Malcolm Jackson
abstract: Contracting skeletal muscles produce reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly hydrogen peroxide, which are essential for exercise-induced adaptations. These ROS activate signaling pathways that promote mitochondrial biogenesis and the expression of key muscle proteins.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Modulates Neutrophil Inflammatory Response to Exercise-Induced Stress
authors: Lucrecia Carrera-Quintanar, Lorena Funes, María Herranz-López, Pascual Martínez-Peinado, Sandra Pasc...
abstract: This study investigated the inflammatory response to exercise and the effect of antioxidant supplements. Antioxidant supplementation appeared to alter neutrophil inflammatory marker release, potentially influencing post-exercise recovery.

title: Physiological and Neural Adaptations to Eccentric Exercise: Mechanisms and Considerations for Training
authors: Nosratollah Hedayatpour, Deborah Falla
abstract: This review examines physiological and neural adaptations to eccentric exercise. It concludes that despite initial damage, eccentric exercise effectively stimulates muscle hypertrophy, increased cortical activity, and improved motor unit function for enhanced muscle performance.

title: Redox correlation in muscle lengthening and immune response in eccentric exercise
authors: Feng He, Chia-Chen Chuang, Tingyang Zhou, Qing Jiang, Darlene A. Sedlock, Li Zuo
abstract: Eccentric exercise in mice and humans was studied for its effects on muscle function and immune cells. Antioxidant supplementation attenuated exercise-induced changes in anti-apoptotic proteins and may protect against muscle dysfunction.

title: Cardioprotection conferred by exercise training is blunted by blockade of the opioid system
authors: Tatiana F G Galvão, Katt C Matos, Patrícia C Brum, Carlos E Negrão, Protásio Lemos da Luz, Antônio C...
abstract: Exercise training and other interventions were studied for their cardioprotective effects. Opioid receptor blockade blunted the cardioprotective benefits of exercise training, suggesting a role for opioids in this protection.

title: Sex differences in the effect of fish-oil supplementation on the adaptive response to resistance exercise training in older people: a randomized controlled trial 1 2
authors: Mariasole Da Boit, Rachael Sibson, Selvaraj Sivasubramaniam, Judith R Meakin, Carolyn A Greig, Richa...
source: The American Journal of Clinical Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated fish oil supplementation's effect on resistance training adaptations in older adults, comparing men and women. Fish oil enhanced muscle strength and quality in women, but not in men, though it lowered triglycerides in both sexes.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blocks Changes in Kynurenine Metabolism Triggered by Three Weeks of Sprint Interval Training in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Ada Trepci, Lilly Schwieler, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Sigitas Kaman...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly men altered kynurenine pathway metabolism towards neuroprotection. This beneficial shift was prevented by concurrent vitamin C and E supplementation.
